Subject: Evidence & custody matrix for model-improvement exclusion

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team has reviewed the platform and we are comfortable in principle with Redwood's isolation controls, but legal needs a concise package to sign off on the DPA addendum for the model-improvement exclusion. Specifically they asked for:  

- A custody matrix that shows where prompt/response data flows (ingest -> ephemeral KV -> logs -> archival) and which systems have read/write access.  
- Evidence that no tenant data is used to improve open-model variants (audit trails, config flags, KMS key usage)
- Proposed transfer/residency plan for archives and a pragmatic SFTP onboarding option for our compliance team to pull evidence if needed.

Can you provide an evidence manifest and a proposed SFTP onboarding checklist (we can engage Paul Chen on your side) by end of week? Legal prefers a short, itemized packet rather than a long narrative.

Alex
Alex Morton
Director of Security Operations
HealthBridge Medical

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Draft evidence manifest + custody matrix (internal)

Folks — I put together the initial evidence_manifest.csv and a one-page custody matrix. Highlights:  

- Ingest path: API -> ephemeral KV cache (tenant-scoped) -> real-time inference engine. Ephemeral KV is configured to TTL 24h (customer-configurable).
- Logging: access logs (tokenized) are written to an internal auditing bucket; we have an ingest label that prevents those logs from being included in model improvement pipelines.
- Model-improvement controls: route-level flag (no_improve=true) enforced at the smart-router; all requests from flagged tenants set an audit tag (improve_exempt) and generate an immutable audit event ID.
- KMS: tenant data keys are tenant-scoped; rotation schedule and use logs are captured in KMS audit events (we can export a usage summary).

Attachments included (internal): evidence_manifest.csv, custody_matrix_1p.pdf, sftp_onboarding.pdf.  

Pending items for legal packet:  
- An export of the last 90 days of KMS usage showing no training pipeline access (David, can you run this and redact as needed?).
- A short operational note that describes how we guarantee the route flag is applied before any KV material is persisted.

I drafted an addendum redline (redline-training-exclusion-addendum.docx) that mirrors the DPA language HealthBridge suggested; Rachel, please review before we share externally.

Kimberly Park
Privacy Ops
Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Rachel — thanks for the packet. We reviewed the custody matrix and the manifest; a few clarifying asks from legal before we can sign the addendum:  

1) Please include the exact audit event IDs and sample entries (redacted) for the route-level flag application and KMS access during the last 30 days. We don't need full logs, but samples that demonstrate the immutable audit trail.
2) Confirm the SFTP onboarding timeline and provide Paul with the host fingerprint and an expected handover date.
3) Add a short paragraph to the addendum clarifying that derivative rights for prompt/response outputs remain with HealthBridge and that Redwood's production telemetry used for platform telemetry (not model training) will be aggregated and irreversible.

If we can get the samples and the SFTP handoff details by Tuesday (09/10), legal can route the addendum for signature the same week.

Best,
Sonia Patel
